note: Diarization is badly fragmented (many '?:' lines) and 20:30-59:30 is Latin-transliterated, so several Latin forms cannot be told apart (e.g. 'Bihteb' is used for Amal's own bit7eb at 25:11). Merger notes: (1) D10 and D24 were mis-paired - r1's D10 half (akun -> 3am baseer, B14) is the SAME row as r2's D24; I kept D10 as r2's aswad->sayyi2 vocab row and D24 as the B14 row, so nothing is doubled. (2) D12/D13: r1 split the 53:36 line into two pieces (ending -ti, preposition bi/fi) and r2 wrote one row covering the preposition; I kept D12 = ending piece (B5) and D13 = preposition piece (D2); r2's D12 half is folded into D13. (3) D17/D32: r1's D17 row is really the laiti piece (= D32); I kept D17 as the haketili piece (r2) and D32 as laiti. (4) D28 (32:30 بيسبت -> بيبسط) and the letter-order part of D15 are the ب/س root-letter swap that READER-BRIEF names as S4 (بنسبت for بنبسط); same slip recurs at 34:21 and 1:01:34. (5) Candidates I did NOT add because they are probably already in the agreed list - please check: 08:36 'بعيد الـ نفس مش الـ' -> 'نفس المشكلة' (A2), 12:54 'el ghayr tariqa' -> 'Not el, just ghayr' (A2), 55:52 'Bi safar hom' -> 'Safartom' (A3), 59:45 'Investii yomek' -> 'Bee Yomeek' (D2), 1:01:23 'الأكتر إشي' -> 'No أل just أكتر إشي' (C3), 1:02:23 'بيسبط' -> 'ببسّط' (B18). Also 04:19-04:26 بهمس/بتحمس -> متحمس (B15) is a separate fix from D19.

row.medi_said: How do you say languages in it? Loka, lokat?
row.why: He tried لقة at 00:39, then asked outright 'How do you say languages' and she supplied لغة; a didn't-know (not on her sheet), the ق/غ sound is S4. r1's word-order piece (software لقة -> لغة الـ software, A2) is dropped: his 00:39 line is too fragmented to prove the order and at 00:59 'Software luka' she was asking what 'software' meant, not fixing order.

rulings.why: Both readers saw the same exchange; the transcript supports the ask (00:55) and her supplying لغة (00:58). The A2 reading rests on a fragmented line and has no signal.

row.medi_said: What language?
row.right: لقيت = you found (شو لقيت؟ = what did you find?)
row.why: She asked شو لقيت؟ twice (01:24, 01:31); he stalled (01:27) then glossed it as 'What language?' (01:34); she said No and unpacked بلاقي / بتلاقي; a sheet word ('you (m) found | inta la2ait | إنت لقيت') read as a different word, so tier 1 not 0.

rulings.why: Same slip in both readers; the transcript shows a wrong identification of a known sheet word (tier 1) and her 'No' (explicit-no), at 01:34.

row.medi_said: To learn would be أتأل-- or يتعلّم
row.why: In 'شو أحسن طريقة ... to learn' he offered the he-form يتعلّم; she said لا, أتعلم (I-form); he then asked 'is that for me or just to learn?' and she said Both - the fix is the person prefix, a bucket rule, so grammar not a didn't-know (he knows the verb: sheet 'i learn | Ana bat3allam').
row.english: the best way (for me) to learn

rulings.why: He did produce a form (يتعلّم) and she rejected it with لا; that is a person-agreement fix, not a new word.

row.medi_said: ووا ال أول مشكلة.
row.why: 'the first problem' is أول مشكلة (idafa, no el- on the first word) or المشكلة الأولى; he put el- on أول; she let it pass as the talk moved to English; low because the line is a fragment and the ال could be a restart.

rulings.why: Real Arabic he said, a bucket rule broken, no signal from her - a grammar-B row at low confidence.

Not an error: سهل كتير (adjective + كتير) is standard Levantine; her 'Ktir sehel?' (13:21) is a rising check of meaning ('too easy?'), followed by her own explanation of why Quizlet is easy, not a recast.

row.why: She asked 'Shu ya3ni muhadatha' (20:31); he could not recall and said 'I don't remember'; she gave the meaning; no wrong word was produced, so it is a didn't-know (tier 0) like D7/D8; sheet 'conversation practice | Mu7aadase | محادثة'.

rulings.why: Same moment in both readers; he produced no wrong word, only a blank, so tier 0 (Amal supplied the meaning), consistent with D7/D8.

row.medi_said: that was zaj. What shuu, shu yanni banzaj?
row.why: She listed the verbs (21:22); he asked the meaning of banzaj and she gave it; sheet 'i get annoyed | Ana banze3ej | أنا بنزعج'; mode listening because he did not produce it, he failed to understand her word (same situation as D6).

row.medi_said: Bahrej. Bahrej. Shu yanni?
row.right: ba7rej = I embarrass; ban7erej = I get embarrassed
row.why: She named bahrej, banherej (21:53); he asked the meaning; sheet 'i embarrass | Ana ba7rej | أنا بحرج' and 'i get embarrassed | Ana ban7erej | أنا بنحرج'; listening for the same reason as D7.

row.medi_said: maruj baru... Is it m-maruj? M-mitruj?
row.why: For 'embarrassed' he offered two participle moulds, maruj (right mould, dropped ح is S4) and mitruj (the mit- mould of متحمس, wrong here); she gave ma7ruj (sheet 'emberrassed | Ma7rooj | محروج'); the mould choice is B15, not a lexical tier-2 slip; low because his first guess was already right.

rulings.why: The wrong piece is which participle pattern to use, which is the B15 rule, not a different form of a noun; his hedge with mit- is the only error, hence low.

row.medi_said: Ana hakeet ma khatibti ashan Arabiyi. Arabiyi, aswad or-
row.why: For 'my Arabic is bad' he said aswad (sheet 'black (m/f) | Aswad | أسود', or a slip toward 'worse | Aswa2 | أسوأ'); she supplied sayyi2 ('bad | Sayyi2 | سيء') and he built on it ('getting worse ... akun sayyi2'); medium because his target word is ambiguous.

rulings.why: The two halves of D10 are different pieces: r1's half (akun -> 3am baseer, B14) is the same row as D24 and is kept there; r2's aswad -> sayyi2 is a real vocab recast and is kept here.

row.medi_said: Inbastat. Huwa, hiya imbastat. Into, hume, imbestu.
row.why: They-form of the past انبسطوا keeps the a-a stem (inbasa6u); he gave the shortened stem imbestu; he then said Imbasatu (51:52, reads as repeating her) and asked 'It's not imbstu?' (51:57), she said Imbasatu again (51:59); medium because the 51:52 line could be a self-fix before her recast.

row.medi_said: this would be embasattet, right? Embassatet il hafla.
row.amal_said: EMBASATI. I need a preposition. What was it? Do you remember?
row.why: 'Did you enjoy the party?' addressed to Amal (f) takes the you-f past ending -ti (she had just given both: 'Embasotet, EMBASOTI' at 53:22); he used -et (I / you-m); she recast EMBASATI before moving to the preposition; the ending is the past-tense person marker (B5).

rulings.why: Both readers quote the same line but r1's row is the ending piece and r2's is the preposition piece; the ending piece is kept here (B5 with B18 as second bucket) and the preposition piece as D13.

row.medi_said: Embassatet il hafla.
row.amal_said: I need a preposition. What was it? Do you remember? ... Bi or fi.
row.why: انبسط takes bi/fi before its object; he said il hafla with no preposition; she prompted 'I need a preposition', he said 'I forget' (53:43), she gave 'Bi or fi' and later both full forms (54:50); he used it at 54:40 (embasati fi el hafleh); sheet 'enjoy (plural) your trip! | Enbes6u bi-re7letkom'.

rulings.why: Both readers actually found this piece (r2 wrote it inside D12); kept once here as the preposition row.

row.medi_said: More, more happy? ... Oh, the most happy. Did you say أحسن or أكثر؟ أحسن right?
row.amal_said: The most. The most. ... شو أكتر إشي. ... No. The best thing is أحسن إشي.
row.why: Her question 'shoo aktar ishi biebsitak' (1:00:46): he read aktar ishi as 'more' (1:01:02), she said 'The most'; he then guessed she had said أحسن (1:01:07) and she said No, شو أكتر إشي, the best thing is أحسن إشي (1:01:15); one listening miss of the sheet item 'the most | Aktar shee | أكتر شيء'.
row.english: what is the thing that makes you happiest?

rulings.why: Both readers describe the same listening miss from different lines; merged into one row anchored at the first wrong reading (1:01:02) with the أحسن follow-up in the quote.

row.medi_said: أكتر إشي بيس– بيسبط–
row.amal_said: بيسبتني- بيب... بي and then س
row.why: 'the thing that makes ME happy' needs the object -ni; her first move was to add it to his word (بيسبتني) before walking him through the letter order; he reached بيبسطني at 1:01:50 (ممتاز); low because his line is cut off (بيسبط–) so he may have been about to add -ni, and the ب/س order part is S4 (brief: بنسبت for بنبسط).
row.english: the thing that makes me happy the most

rulings.why: Only r1 wrote it; she did supply the -ni, but his line is cut mid-word, so real-but-unprovable, kept at low.

row.medi_said: عافيا فيكي. شكرًا.
row.why: Reply to her يعطيك العافية (1:03:03) is the set phrase الله يعافيكي; he produced a made-up shape of the same word (عافية/يعافي), so a wrong form of a word he knows (tier 2) rather than a different word; she let it pass; the reply is not on her sheet (only 'ya'tiki al'afyah | يعطيكي العافية').

rulings.why: Both readers agree it is vocab-B and low; the transcript shows a mangled form of the right word, which the brief files as tier 2.

row.medi_said: when I tell you about what I found.
row.right: lama haketili = when you (f) told me
row.why: In her sentence 'Basatini lama haketili innek laiti shughal' (41:19) he read haketili as 'I tell you' (41:57 'when you talk about', 42:07 'when I tell you'), flipping the you-f past ending -ti and the -li (to me); she repeated 'Lama haketilli' until he got 'when you told me' (42:15).

rulings.why: r1's D17 row is really the laiti piece (its why is about 41:34/41:57), which is D32; the haketili flip at 42:07 is a distinct piece and is kept here.

Not an error: he said الطريق منيح - a masculine noun with a masculine adjective, which agrees; she fixed only the noun (طريق أو طريقة؟, the agreed row) and he answered طريقة without ever re-saying the adjective, so 'طريقة منيح' was never spoken.

row.medi_said: I excited؟ أنا بهمس.
row.why: For 'I am excited' he asked 'Do I excite myself or am I excited?' then committed to the make-form بهمس (ba7ammes, dropped ح is S4); she recast the get-form بتحمس (sheet 'i get excited | Ana bat7ammas | أنا بتحمس'); her later fix to متحمس (04:19-04:26) is a separate B15 row.

rulings.why: Only r2 wrote it; the transcript shows the make/get swap and her recast plainly, before the later participle fix.

Not tier 3: 'an easy answer, I should say' is a whole English clause, a meta aside refining what he had just said; he then produced جواب, paused, she supplied سهل - a pause fill (S5), and he knew the word (13:16 'sehel ktir').

row.medi_said: ahana shay na'na' ma asal mufrad. Al-muftadi wa mufrad-
row.why: Answering 'Bihteb asal?' he said mint tea with honey 'mufrad' (singular / alone) for 'only / no sugar'; she did not follow ('Anja?') and guessed 'Mesh sukkar?', which he confirmed; she never corrected the word; low because the Latin transcript of this line is garbled.
row.english: mint tea with honey only, no sugar

rulings.why: Only r2 wrote it; her 'Anja? Mesh sukkar?' shows the word failed, but she guessed the meaning rather than fixing it, so vocab-B at low.

Cannot be verified: the Latin transcript writes Amal's own بتحب as 'Bihteb' at 25:11 ('Bihteb asal?'), so his 'khatibti bih teb' is most likely the same بتحب, i.e. correct; nothing shows a masculine بيحب.

row.medi_said: Ana hakeet ma khatibti ashan Arabiyi.

row.english: I talked with my fiancée about my Arabic

rulings.why: Only r2 wrote it; a plausible wrong word with no signal, kept as vocab-B at low with the alternative reading stated.

row.medi_said: getting worse so she would it be akun, akunsayye'?
row.why: 'Is getting worse' is a change in progress: 3am + baseer (I am becoming) + sayyi2; he offered akun (I be); she recast 3am baseer sayyi2 and he repeated it (26:46 'Baseer, yeah, baseer sayyi2').

rulings.why: Both readers found this (r1's half of D10 is the same row); kept once here as B14 with recast.

row.medi_said: Qeem kamar marra?
row.amal_said: Eem kamman el el esot eem. Eem Ana baqim.
row.why: She said 'bedna n2eemha' (remove the N, 28:22) and asked shu ya3ni; he answered 'Kam marra?' (28:29) and again heard 'qeem kaman' as 'kam marra' (28:56); she explained 'Ana baqim' (sheet 'i remove / take away | Ba2eem | بقيم'); low because the Latin transcript of this stretch is garbled.

rulings.why: Only r2 wrote it; the transcript shows he could not place her verb 2eem twice and she supplied the meaning; kept as a didn't-know at low.

Not an error: 'Does it go back to the و?' (30:58) is an open question about the stem vowel of the present, not a form he asserted; she answered لا / ما بزيد and he produced babset (31:06) at once; the stem vowel is not a grammar bucket (F-series is sound shape) and B12 (make vs get) is not what was at issue.

row.medi_said: It makes me happy مضارع present tense امmm so this is with an right؟
row.amal_said: Which n لا ليش؟ We're still in this verb we haven't took–we haven't taken any other verbs.
row.why: 'It makes me happy' is the make-form (بسّط); he proposed the N (get-form انبسط) with 'right?'; she said لا, we are still in this verb; he then produced بيسبت/بيبسطني (32:30-33:04).

rulings.why: Only r2 wrote it; unlike D26 he asserted a wrong form ('with an N, right?') and she rejected it, which is the B12 confusion.

S4 by the brief's own example: بيسبت for بيبسط is the ب/س root-letter swap that READER-BRIEF lists as pronunciation ('a root letter slip (بنسبت for بنبسط)'); the same slip recurs at 34:21 (بنسبت -> بنبسط) and 1:01:34, and her 'two Bs' explanation is her way of walking the sounds, not a b- prefix rule (his form kept the بي prefix).

row.medi_said: sorry هية بتيبست- يبستوا and احنا بين- بينبست.
row.why: In the present run (إنت بتيبست، إنتي بتيبستي، أنتو بتيبستو، هو بيبست) the they-form came out as يبستوا with no b- prefix; she moved on to احنا (34:19) without fixing it; low because the dropped ب may be a transcription artefact in a run of stumbles.

rulings.why: Only r2 wrote it; a bucket rule (B1) broken in a produced form with no signal - grammar-B at low.

row.medi_said: Did i make you... اه بسات- بساتِ- بساتِتني أسف بساتِتك.
row.why: 'Did I make you happy' = basatt-ak: the I-past -et loses its vowel before the object -ak; he kept it (basatit-ak); the 36:05 '?:' line echoes his form and recasts بَسْتَكْ (Amal by content), and he asked 'do I remove the ET? Ok بسَتَّكْ' (36:13).

rulings.why: Only r2 wrote it; the recast line is unlabeled but is clearly hers (he answers it), and his 36:13 line confirms the fix.

row.medi_said: basati is she, she makes happy right?
row.amal_said: No,- Or you make happy female ...that's you. You make happy.
row.why: Listing his four -ti/-i forms (38:58) he assigned basati (بسّطتي, you-f past) to 'she'; she said No, that is you (f); a past-ending person error in his own paradigm, so speaking not listening.

rulings.why: Only r2 wrote it; he produced the form and glossed the ending wrongly, she said No - real B5 row; mode set to speaking because it is his own form, not her Arabic misread.

row.medi_said: hold on. These words are jumbling together now this is problem. Laeit, laeit mal
row.why: In 'Basatini lama haketili innek laiti shughal' (41:19) he could not place laiti and stalled; she explained balaa2i and repeated the sentence until he got 'when you find work' (41:50) and 'laiti is you found' (42:31); sheet 'you (f) found | inti la2aiti | إنتي لقيتي'; r1's D17 row is this same piece.

rulings.why: Real listening miss; r1 also saw it (its D17 why) so both readers found it; kept once here.

row.medi_said: And about you.
row.why: Going word by word she said 'Innekh' (42:17); he glossed it 'about you'; she glossed 'that you' and he repeated innek (42:25); inno + -ek ending read as a preposition phrase; low because it is one word in a word-by-word parse.

rulings.why: Only r2 wrote it; the misgloss and her fix are both on the page, kept at low.

Not a distinct error: the 42:50 line is a whole-sentence read-back paraphrase ('I'm happy that you told me you found work'); its pieces are already D17 (haketili), D32 (laiti) and D33 (innek), he had rendered basatini correctly as 'you made me happy' at 41:09 and confirmed it at 43:03, and she restated the sentence without a no.

row.medi_said: Y- you don't put a E, right? It's just بسّت؟ بستي؟ بستي، بستو.
row.amal_said: No. ليش ما منحط إي بدنا إي ... بست. إبست We do need an E. ... No, because it's three consonants or more.
row.why: The command of بسّط needs the initial i- (إبسّط) because the stem has three consonants; he asserted no E and gave بسّت، بستي، بستو; she said No and named the rule (44:04 'three consonants or more'); he then gave ابست، ابستي، ابسطو (44:25, ✓).

rulings.why: Only r2 wrote it; explicit No plus a named rule on the page.
